method: Twelve-app source audit covering all ten categories. Five material claims per app were compared with the stored excerpts fetched from official documentation. Partial or unsupported claims count as misses.
scope: Evidence agreement, not a global factual-accuracy estimate for all 100 apps.

apps.finding: The draft bundled OAuth into a description without matching evidence and inferred a paid-plan requirement that the source did not prove.
The sampled authentication, access, API, MCP and buildability claims matched the fetched official excerpts.
The draft description generalized beyond the messaging products established by the supplied source.
OAuth, developer-token review, REST and RPC access, and official MCP claims matched the official documentation sample.
The sampled final claims were directly supported after the retry produced a structurally valid draft.
The draft mistook a curl example for a product CLI and assigned API breadth more confidently than the source allowed.
OAuth-token evidence was insufficient to classify the sampled authentication path specifically as OAuth 2.0.
An OAuth-flow reference did not explicitly establish the stricter OAuth 2.0 enum used by the schema.
The Business or Enterprise plan restriction and integration claims matched the fetched official evidence.
Variable pricing and contact-sales evidence did not prove the draft's stronger paid-plan classification.
Enterprise setup, licence and Google Cloud role requirements were supported by the official documentation.
The repository established a usable local CLI with no remote credential requirement.
